notes.units: Every length is a fraction of the foot length (0.2581 m for the reference subject); positions run from the heel back (0) to the toe tip (1).
notes.toe_spring: [start, tip rise, exponent]. 7.0 mm at the reference length. It starts ahead of the toe contact sphere (0.937 of the length) so the drawn sole stays within 2 mm of that sphere's lowest point; a dress last's toe spring is commonly quoted as 10 to 15 mm, which this model cannot reach without leaving the contact sphere. Modelling parameter, not a measurement.
notes.heel_height, forefoot_height: Top of the sole edge above the ground: 22.0 mm at the heel (the sole thickness used since #15280) and 11.6 mm under the ball. Modelling parameters.
notes.sole_slope: [from, to]: the sole top falls from the heel height to the forefoot height over this span.
notes.shank: [from, to, blend, lift, cover]: the sole underside is lifted 4.9 mm between the heel breast and the ball, which separates the heel from the forefoot; the upper stays cover times that lift above the ground there. Modelling parameter.
notes.insole: Underside of the upper above the ground (0.8 mm), so the sole alone is seen from below.
notes.welt: The sole edge stands 4.0 mm outside the upper (3.0 mm before #15299). Modelling parameter.
notes.sole_edge_exponent: Super-ellipse exponent of the sole section: 8 gives a flat welt ledge and upright edge.
notes.heel_counter, saddle, toe_cap: [.. span .., proud]: stitched-on panels drawn 1.0 to 1.5 mm outside the upper; the heel counter and saddle take the saddle material and the toe cap is its seam, a narrow raised band. Modelling parameters.
notes.laces: [count, lace width, share of the shoe width, proud of the saddle, mesh stations].
notes.panel_floor: Underside of a panel as a share of the sole-edge height, which hides it inside the sole.
notes.panel_stations, max_vertices: Mesh density of a panel and the vertex budget of one foot (ankle stub, bare foot, upper, sole and panels).
